lines.text: Doctor Strange looked into fourteen million, six hundred and five futures.
He told Tony Stark they win in exactly one.
He lied.
There were two. And he hid the second one for a reason.
This is Avengers: Endgame. With the future Strange never told us about.
It starts with the worst day in history. Thanos snaps his fingers, and half of all life turns to dust.
On a quiet farm, Clint Barton turns around. His family is gone.
Tony Stark is adrift in space, out of air, recording a goodbye.
Part of the journey is the end.
Then a light appears outside the window. Captain Marvel carries the whole ship home.
The Avengers find Thanos on a garden planet, and demand the stones. But he has already destroyed them.
The work is done. It always will be.
Thor takes his head. And it changes nothing.
Five years pass. The world doesn't move on. It just gets quieter.
Steve runs a support group. Natasha runs what is left of the Avengers. And Thor stops answering the door.
Tony has a cabin, a lake, and a daughter named Morgan.
I love you three thousand.
Then a rat walks across a dashboard in a storage unit, and Scott Lang falls out of the quantum realm.
For him, it wasn't five years. It was five hours. Which means time works differently down there.
Which means, a time machine.
Tony says no. Then, at midnight, he does the math. And it works.
I figured it out, by the way.
The plan is a heist. Six stones, three teams, one trip each.
New York, twenty twelve. Steve has to fight himself, and wins with a whisper.
Asgard. Thor sees his mother one last time. And his hammer still comes when he calls.
Morag. Nebula's memories leak across time. And the Thanos of the past sees everything.
And Vormir. A cliff, a stone, and a price. A soul, for a soul.
Natasha and Clint fight each other for the right to fall. Natasha wins.
They come home with six stones, and one empty space on the platform.
Bruce puts on the gauntlet. It nearly burns his arm off. But he snaps.
Birds return to the trees. Clint's phone rings. It's his wife.
Then the sky opens, and a warship from twenty fourteen turns the compound into a crater.
Thanos is back. And this time, he isn't here for half.
I will shred this universe down to its last atom.
Three Avengers walk out to meet him. Iron Man. Thor. Captain America.
They lose. Thor is pinned. And then the hammer lifts off the ground, and flies into Steve's hand.
I knew it!
It isn't enough. The shield breaks. And Steve stands alone, against an army.
And then, a voice in his ear.
On your left.
A portal opens. Then another. Then hundreds.
Wakanda. Asgard. The wizards. The Guardians. The kid from Queens. Everyone who turned to dust, walks back.
Avengers. Assemble.
The gauntlet crosses the battlefield like a football. Clint. T'Challa. Peter. Carol.
Thanos gets it anyway. Tony looks at Strange. And Strange raises one finger.
You know this part. Tony steals the stones. Says four words. And saves the universe with his life.
I am Iron Man.
That is the one future Strange showed us.
Here is the one he didn't.
In the second future, Strange doesn't raise one finger. He raises his whole hand, open.
And Tony understands. He isn't supposed to carry it alone.
He takes the stones. The power tears through his arm. And before he can snap, Steve grabs his shoulder.
Together.
Then Thor takes Steve's arm. Carol takes Thor's. Peter. Bruce. Wanda. T'Challa. Hand over hand, across the whole battlefield.
The Guardians did this once, with one stone. This is six stones, and every hero on Earth.
I am inevitable.
And we, are the Avengers.
They snap. Together.
Thanos turns to dust. His army turns to dust. And Tony Stark opens his eyes.
He goes home. He walks up the steps of the cabin. And Morgan gets her dad back.
I love you three thousand.
But this is why Strange hid it. Power shared, is power spent.
Thor reaches for the lightning, and nothing comes. Carol's light goes out. Peter can't feel the danger anymore. And Steve looks down, at an old man's hands.
They saved everyone. And it cost every one of them the thing that made them Avengers.
Strange saw this future. A world where Tony Stark lives, and nobody is left to answer the call.
And in the dark, far past the edge of the map, something notices.
So. One hero's life, or every hero's power? Comment Tony, or powers.
And tell us what to reimagine next.
Titanic, where the door fits two? The Matrix, where Neo takes the blue pill? Or The Dark Knight, where the Joker tells the truth?
The top comment gets made. And send this to the friend who still isn't over Tony Stark.
